title: Why the sky is blue: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: Sunlight has only one color inside it.
We can see the air around the Earth.
The air has very tiny molecules.
In the evening, the sky can be orange, pink, or red.
When the Sun is low, sunlight travels through less air.
What does sunlight have inside it?
What do scientists call the spreading of blue light?
Which light spreads in many directions when sunlight hits the air?
items.why: “When sunlight hits them, blue light spreads in many directions.”

options: Because much of the blue light scatters away
Because the Sun is red in the evening
Because there is no air in the evening

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Sunlight looks white, but it has many colors inside it. When sunlight hits the tiny molecules in the air, blue light spreads in many directions. That is why the sky looks blue.
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue and violet.
When sunlight hits the tiny molecules in the air, blue light spreads in many directions. Scientists call this scattering.

items.q: Why can the sky be orange, pink or red in the evening?
items.model: When the Sun is low, sunlight travels through more air. Much of the blue light scatters away before it reaches us.

items.q: What color is the sky where you live today? What color is it in the evening?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the ideas in the order of the text.
items: Sunlight looks white but has many colors
Tiny molecules in the air scatter blue light
In the evening, much of the blue light scatters away
